source_text: In catholica enim ecclesia, ut omittam sincerissimam sapientiam, ad cuius cognitionem pauci spiritales in hac uita perueniunt, ut eam ex minima quidem parte, quia homines sunt, sed tamen sine dubitatione cognoscant — ceteram quippe turbam non intellegendi uiuacitas, sed credendi simplicitas tutissimam facit — ut ergo hanc omittam sapientiam, quam in ecclesia esse catholica non creditis. multa sunt alia, quae in eius gremio me iustissime teneant. tenet consensio populorum atque gentium; tenet auctoritas miraculis inchoata, spe nutrita, caritate aucta, uetustate firmata; tenet ab ipsa sede Petri apostoli, cui pascendas oues suas post resurrectionem dominus commendauit, usque ad praesentem episcopatum successio sacerdotum; tenet postremo ipsum catholicae nomen. quod non sine causa inter tam multas haereses sic ista ecclesia sola obtinuit. ut cum omnes haeretici se catholicos dici uelint, quaerenti tamen alicui peregrino, ubi ad catholicam conueniatur, nullus haereticorum uel basilicam suam uel domum audeat ostendere. ista ergo tot et tanta nominis christiani carissima uincula recte hominem tenent credentem in catholica ecclesia, etiamsi propter nostrae intellegentiae tarditatem uel uitae meritum ueritas nondum se apertissime ostendat. apud uos autem, ubi nihil horum est, quod me inuitet ac teneat, sola personat pollicitatio ueritatis: quae quidem si tam manifesta monstratur, ut in dubium uenire non possit, praeponenda est illis omnibus rebus, quibus in catholica teneor; si autem tantummodo promittitur et non exhibetur, nemo me mouebit ab ea fide, quae animum meum tot et tantis nexibus christianae religioni astringit.
thought_title: What holds me in the Catholic Church
orientation: Augustine is addressing the Manichaeans, explaining why he remains in the Catholic Church before he examines Mani's Fundamental Letter.
pass_a_gloss: In [the] catholic indeed church, as I may omit [the] most sincere wisdom, to [the] knowledge of which [the] few spiritual [ones] in this life arrive, so that it from [the] least indeed part, because men they are, but nevertheless without doubt they may know — [the] rest indeed crowd not [the] liveliness of understanding, but [the] simplicity of believing most safe makes — as therefore this I may omit wisdom, which in [the] church to be catholic not you believe. many are other [things], which in her bosom me most justly hold. holds [the] agreement of peoples and of nations; holds [the] authority by miracles begun, by hope nourished, by charity increased, by old age strengthened; holds from [the] very seat of Peter [the] apostle, to whom [the] sheep of him to be fed after [the] resurrection [the] Lord entrusted, up to [the] present episcopate [the] succession of priests; holds lastly [the] very of catholic [the] name. which not without cause among so many heresies thus this church alone has obtained. so that when all heretics themselves catholic to be called wish, to [one] asking nevertheless any foreigner, where to [the] catholic [church] it is assembled, none of [the] heretics either [the] basilica of him or [the] house dares to show. these therefore so many and so great of [the] Christian name dearest bonds rightly [a] man hold believing in [the] catholic church, even if because of our of understanding [the] slowness or of life [the] merit [the] truth not yet herself most openly shows. among you however, where nothing of these is, which me may invite and hold, alone sounds [the] promise of truth: which indeed if so manifest is shown, that into doubt to come not it can, to be preferred is to all those [things], by which in [the] catholic [church] I am held; if however only is promised and not is exhibited, no one me will move from that faith, which [the] soul of me [with] so many and so great bonds to [the] Christian religion binds.

choices.why: Keeps the superlative force of sincerissimam and the glossary sense of wisdom as spiritual knowledge; 'sincere' preserves the Latin root meaning of pure and unmixed.
Renders the abstract noun literally; Augustine contrasts intellectual quickness with simple faith.
Preserves the superlative and the literal sense of safety from error.

choices.english: the agreement of peoples and nations
choices.why: Literal rendering of both nouns; 'peoples' and 'nations' are distinct terms in Latin and both should appear.
rejected: the consensus of peoples and nations

choices.why: Keeps the superlative and the metaphor of bonds or chains, which Augustine uses throughout the passage.

choices.english: only the promise of truth sounds aloud
choices.why: Personat means to sound loudly or resound; the literal sense conveys that the Manichaeans have nothing but a loud promise.
rejected: only the promise of truth resounds
only the promise of truth is heard

pass_b_english: For in the Catholic Church—to say nothing of the most sincere wisdom, to the knowledge of which few spiritual people attain in this life, so that they know it at least in part, because they are human, but still without doubt; for the rest of the crowd, it is not liveliness of understanding but simplicity of believing that makes them most safe—to say nothing, then, of this wisdom, which you do not believe is in the Catholic Church, there are many other things that most justly hold me in her bosom. The agreement of peoples and nations holds me; the authority begun by miracles, nourished by hope, increased by love, and made firm by age holds me; the succession of priests from the very seat of the apostle Peter, to whom the Lord after his resurrection entrusted his sheep to be fed, down to the present episcopate holds me; and finally, the very name Catholic holds me, which not without reason this Church alone has obtained among so many heresies, so that although all heretics want to be called catholic, when some stranger asks where the Catholic Church gathers, no heretic dares to point to his own basilica or house. These, then, so many and so great, are the dearest bonds of the Christian name that rightly hold a person believing in the Catholic Church, even if, because of the slowness of our understanding or the merit of our life, the truth does not yet show itself most openly. But among you, where there is none of this to invite and hold me, only the promise of truth sounds aloud. If that truth is shown so clearly that it cannot come into doubt, it is to be preferred to all those things by which I am held in the Catholic Church. But if it is merely promised and not delivered, no one will move me from that faith which binds my soul to the Christian religion by so many and such great ties.
